body:
I mentioned this when reviewing the PR #106863 :
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/106863#discussion_r2113153209
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/106863#issuecomment-2933579128

Obviously moving this stuff around can cause regressions, imo at least the non-physics interpolated case should be changed back to work with the previous method.

_(I didn't do this in the end because I was concerned about avoiding becoming maintainer for this area 😁 .)_

Maybe @simpkins might be interested.

Just brainstorming about the right long term solution here:

- Regardless of whether we have to revert this in the short term, the old SoftBody3D logic of doing work in `frame_pre_draw` doesn't really seem like the right thing for SoftBody3D to do. The physics server re-computes soft body state once per physics frame, and it seems like SoftBody3D's updates should be tied to the physics frame loop. Additionally, the updates done in `frame_pre_draw` are currently racy and hang/crash when the physics server is running on a separate thread (#105195). It does seem better for `SoftBody3D` to do its updates in the physics process iteration.

- However, SkeletonModifier3D appears to make it difficult for other nodes to see up-to-date information in the physics process cycle. If I understand the code correctly `BoneAttachment3D` will never return up-to-date bone positions during _process_physics(), even when the `Skeleton3D's` `modifier_callback_mode_process` is set to `MODIFIER_CALLBACK_MODE_PROCESS_PHYSICS`: the skeleton modifiers are always run as part of a separate deferred `NOTIFICATION_UPDATE_SKELETON` notification that only runs after `NOTIFICATION_INTERNAL_PHYSICS_PROCESS` has been delivered to all other nodes (including nodes with a higher `process_physics_priority` value).

This sort of feels like it might be a more general issue with `BoneAttachment3D` not reflecting skeleton modifier updates during the physics frame?

>Regardless of whether we have to revert this in the short term, the old SoftBody3D logic of doing work in frame_pre_draw doesn't really seem like the right thing for SoftBody3D to do. The physics server re-computes soft body state once per physics frame, and it seems like SoftBody3D's updates should be tied to the physics frame loop. Additionally, the updates done in frame_pre_draw are currently racy and hang/crash when the physics server is running on a separate thread (SoftBody3D crashes game when "physics/3d/run_on_separate_thread" is on #105195). It does seem better for SoftBody3D to do its updates in the physics process iteration.

~Physics process is only used when physics interpolation enabled. We always use process to update mesh. So maybe it just need to change process to frame_pre_draw?~ 

But anyway, using frame_pre_draw feels like a hack. As users usually only use process and physics process, so a better solution would be preferable.

> Physics process is only used when physics interpolation enabled. We always use process to update mesh.

I think you maybe have it backwards?  The code calls `_update_soft_mesh()` in physics process, which is what is intended to get updates from the physics server.  It the publishes the changes to the `RenderingServer` in physics process when interpolation is off, or in process when interpolation is on:

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/efb40c1524e54f2cf52f213e248bd0a7b790975a/scene/3d/physics/soft_body_3d.cpp#L350-L361

Note that when `physics/3d/run_on_separate_thread` is enabled, SoftBody3D cannot get mesh updates back from the physics server immediately: the physics logic runs on another thread and so it takes some time between when we send the pinned points updates and when we can get back updated positions.  (In theory we could block waiting for a response from the physics thread, even if we didn't want to wait for the next physics frame cycle, but this is not great from a performance perspective, and opens ourself up to more places where deadlocks can occur if anyone else needs work done on the main thread while we are blocked on the physics thread.)

If we need pinned vertices to be exactly up-to-date, I think the right thing to do would be to have SoftBody3D also update these vertices directly in its vertex buffer when it sends the new positions to the physics server, so their locations are up-to-date immediately without having to wait for the next frame update from the physics server.  Note that in order to do this correctly SoftBody3D would need to know the mapping between render vertices and physics vertices, so it can update all affected render vertices.  (See #108149 for a bit more explanation about the mapping from render vertices to physics vertices.)

One possible thought for a fix would be:
- Add some sort of enum flag to control when SoftBody3D processes pinned point attachments (sort of similar to `Skeleton3D`'s `modifier_callback_mode_process`  flag?).  This would control when we invoke `SoftBody3D::_update_physics_server()`.  The options could be something like:
  - During `process`
  - During `physics_process`
  - Only invoke manually (and provide a function for users to invoke to trigger this)
  - After `MODIFIER_CALLBACK_MODE_PROCESS_PHYSICS` SkeletonModifiers have run?  (This seems like what might be desired in this case.  It would probably take some thought to figure out how we implement this, though.)
- Update `SoftBody3D::_update_physics_server()` to also immediately update positions in the mesh vertex buffer in addition to calling `PhysicsServer3D::soft_body_move_point()`.  This way these vertex positions immediately reflect the new locations without needing to fetch vertex positions back from the physics server.  Doing this does require knowledge of the mapping from render vertices to physics vertices, and back.

I've got some code at https://github.com/simpkins/godot/tree/soft_body where I have been prototyping implementing godotengine/godot-proposals#12670, and this code does have the render-to-physics vertex mapping available in SoftBody3D now.  (For this issue we might need to update it to also store the reverse mapping.  Maybe for each `PinnedPoint` we could just store a list of all render vertices that it affects.  That would perhaps also help to fix #108149.)

I made a pretty hacky proof-of-concept just to experiment with what this approach would look like: simpkins/godot@2b36d4f6

This code:
- moves the pinned point updates from physics_process to process
- also updates the mesh vertex buffer alongside the calls to `PhysicsServer3D::soft_body_move_point()`

This prototype doesn't correctly update all render vertices associated with the pinned point, but that works fine for the MRP here, since it is a simple cloth-like mesh with exactly 1 render vertex per physics vertex.

If I set `modifier_callback_mode_process` to "Physics" on the Skeleton3D then this change does appear to fix the gap between the soft body and the wing bones.  (I believe this change is needed because then the skeleton modifier will run after physics_process and before process, which then allows the SoftBody3D code to see up-to-date values in process.)  When using this `modifier_callback_mode_process` setting the wing bones to temporarily render at their idle position for 1 frame when hitting space, but the soft body is unaffected.  It looks like that doesn't happen in 4.4.1, but I didn't debug what the difference is there.  (It seems like it might be some other change not related to SoftBody3D?)

Also, maybe cc @TokageItLab regarding when BoneAttachment3D values are expected to have up-to-date values when affected by SkeletonModifier3D.  (Specifically my comments above: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/108209#issuecomment-3030319115)

Some great stuff here 👍 , particularly coming up towards the same solution when I looked at this last month.

In the interests of giving some ideas, I've made that experimental branch into a draft so you guys can see what I was thinking at the time #108229 . Feel free to copy any ideas.
FYI, now Godot has [ModifierBoneTarget3D](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/106846) separate from BoneAttachment3D to obtain modified transforms.

> FYI, now Godot has [ModifierBoneTarget3D](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/106846) separate from BoneAttachment3D to obtain modified transforms.

I might be misunderstanding, but I'm not sure that `ModifierBoneTarget3D` looks like it would help here.  It looks like that class will help if the transform needs to be used by another `SkeletonModifier3D`, but `SoftBody3D` is just a regular node, not a skeleton modifier.  If I understand correctly, `ModifierBoneTarget3D` will still give the old transform if read in physics_process or process.

I suppose one option we could do is keep using the `frame_pre_draw` notification to read bone transforms as late as possible, just before things get rendered.  In the `frame_pre_draw` handler we could read the attachment transforms and only update the local mesh buffers, without sending the data to the physics server.  We still send attachment transforms to the physics server in `physics_process`.  This avoids sending unnecessary updates to the physics server multiple times per physics frame, and it also ensures that the pinned points are in the correct location just before we render.  This does feel slightly weird, since the physics server would still be doing the next step based on one frame out-of-date positions.  The pinned points would be up-to-date, but their neighbors would be getting computed from slightly laggy data.  This would probably still look okay, though?

> FYI, now Godot has [ModifierBoneTarget3D](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/106846) separate from BoneAttachment3D to obtain modified transforms.

Thanks! Although the lag is still present, this solves the glitch with SoftBody using AnimationPlayer's pose instead of the override.

> The pinned points would be up-to-date, but their neighbors would be getting computed from slightly laggy data.

This is something that have been happening before physics interpolation was supported by SoftBody, as I described in #107061. It becomes more apparent at higher speeds, when free vertices may begin to overlap pinned vertices, which messes up the calculation of normals as a result.

Just to be clear - I am not currently working on this, I believe this is @simpkins / @beicause area.

(Although I've chipped in, I'm actively avoiding this as I already have far too much to maintain / work on, and this isn't strictly speaking physics interpolation, this is general soft body maintenance, and there's still quite a bit of work I can foresee to be done in this area).

I'm not working on anything for the 4.5 timeframe.

I'm not really sure what the preferred change would be for a short term resolution.  The interpolation-related changes that moved processing from the `frame_pre_draw` callback into `_physics_process()` seem "correct" to me from a physics perspective, in that we should really be updating the physics server in physics_process, between physics steps.  SoftBody3D is rather unfortunate in that it currently mixes both physics processing and rendering behavior, and things end up being weird when you want to try and make this physics object map precisely to other objects that are animated in `_process()` frames, or whose updates come only after `_physics_process()` has finished.  In the long run I think it would be ideal to replace SoftBody3D with some separate classes that more clearly separate physics logic from code that uses the physics simulation to update rendered meshes.  In the medium-term we could fix up some of the SoftBody3D behavior to update the physics server in `_physics_process()` while also updating pinned render vertices each `_process()` frame.  However, in the short term this is a bit challenging since some of the render logic is currently happening inside PhysicsServer3D, and SoftBody3D itself doesn't contain all the data needed to update its render vertices.

Well, if no one is going to work on fixing this for 4.5 we need to revert https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/106863 and then come back with a more proper solution for 4.6 (perhaps building off of the POC that @simpkins made in https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/108209#issuecomment-3030574089)
